title: MWCD and MSDE to jointly launch NAVYA 2.0 in Haridwar on 28 November 2026
subtitle: Joint initiative to empower adolescent girls and young women through skills, confidence-building and livelihood opportunities across 100 districts in 24 States/UTs
body_text: The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) will jointly launch the second phase of NAVYA – Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls (NAVYA 2.0) on 28 November 2026 at 3:30 PM at the Uttarakhand Sanskrit Academy Auditorium, Haridwar. Building on the learnings of its pilot phase, NAVYA 2.0 aims to advance women-led development by nurturing the aspirations of adolescent girls and young women, strengthening their capabilities and enabling them to achieve greater confidence, self-reliance and economic independence. The programme will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development; Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Smt. Rekha Arya, Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Mandan Kaushik, Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; and Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand. The launch programme will feature the formal launch of NAVYA 2.0 by the Union Ministers. It will also include the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand, and distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY). NAVYA: Nurturing aspirations and enabling empowerment NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of MWCD and MSDE that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women. The initiative recognises that empowerment goes beyond training and entails nurturing aspirations, building confidence, developing capabilities and enabling informed choices about the future. The pilot phase was launched on 24 June 2025 in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, with an envisaged coverage of 27 Aspirational Districts across 19 States. Approximately 1,200 adolescent girls were trained in industry-relevant job roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Solar PV Installation Helper and Fashion Designer. The initiative also emphasised digital and financial literacy, career readiness and entrepreneurship to strengthen their confidence and socio-economic independence. NAVYA 2.0: Expanding the horizons of empowerment Building on the pilot experience, NAVYA 2.0 will expand its reach to 100 districts across 24 States/UTs, with a particular focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. The eligible age group has also been widened from 16–18 years to 16–25 years, bringing a larger cohort of adolescent girls and young women within its ambit. The expanded initiative will provide greater access to vocational training in industry-relevant, new-age and non-traditional job roles, while strengthening pathways to employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. It places emphasis on institutional convergence, coordinated district-level implementation and outcome-oriented support. A structured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to facilitate effective coordination and implementation at the district level. Technology-enabled implementation The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) will serve as the digital platform for facilitating access to skilling opportunities and supporting candidates throughout their journey from enrolment to training and certification. It will also enable real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress and certification, strengthening transparency and accountability. Digitally verifiable credentials will further help candidates demonstrate their skills and competencies. Advancing women-led development Through the convergence of MWCD and MSDE, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, pursue their aspirations and participate meaningfully in economic and social development. NAVYA 2.0 is a step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment, enabling every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat. *** SH
